text: January's depreciation run processes every asset in LTV US Corporate Book — including FA-10452, exactly as it was capitalized. This lesson turns last lesson's category mistake into a precise, calculable number.

As configured: $145,000 cost, Office Equipment's 5-year life, 60 months — $145,000 divided by 60 is $2,416.67 a month. As it should be: Manufacturing Equipment's 10-year life, 120 months — $145,000 divided by 120 is $1,208.33 a month.

The gap is $1,208.34 for January alone, booked to cost center 410 instead of 420. The run doesn't fail or look unusual — depreciation posts, Create Accounting picks it up, and the amount lands in the General Ledger looking like any other properly calculated charge.

This isn't a one-time error. It repeats every month the asset stays miscategorized — one month deep by the time Chapter 3 investigates, but it would compound past fourteen thousand dollars over a full year if it went uncaught. That's exactly why catching it at the first month-end matters.
